description: Key references for FlyWire + embodied AI research and internship application. URLs verified May 2026.

sources.title: FlyWire: online community for whole-brain connectomics
sources.notes: Core FlyWire platform paper. Describes EM pipeline, browser-based 3D segmentation, collaborative proofreading, and mechanosensory circuit analysis. Foundation for understanding FlyWire data schema and annotation pipeline. Read first.

sources.title: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain
sources.notes: Complete wiring diagram: 139,255 proofread neurons, >50M synaptic connections. Companion papers include Schlegel et al. (hierarchical cell-type annotation) and others. Use to identify sensorimotor subgraph for Project A.

sources.title: Network statistics of the whole-brain connectome of Drosophila
sources.key_findings: 130,000+ neurons; rich-club organization; ~30% neurons are high-degree hubs; hierarchy and community structure quantified on v630 snapshot.
sources.notes: Primary methodological reference for Project A. Shows exactly the metrics (degree, betweenness, hierarchy, modularity) we replicate in the toy notebook.

sources.title: flywire-network-analysis: analysis scripts + Zenodo data package
sources.notes: Public scripts and data snapshots accompanying Lin et al. 2024. Python graph-tool based (Linux/Mac). Migrate minimal_structural_analysis.ipynb logic to this dataset for real Project A analysis.

sources.title: FlyWire Whole-brain Connectome Connectivity Data
sources.notes: Public snapshot of FlyWire connectivity data. Direct replacement for toy_connectome CSV files in Project A notebook.

sources.title: murthylab/codex: FlyWire Connectome Data Explorer
sources.notes: Web app + Python library for querying FlyWire neurons, annotations, connectivity. Primary programmatic access portal. Use for subsetting sensorimotor neurons for Project A.

sources.title: Whole-Brain Connectomic Graph Model Enables Whole-Body Locomotion Control in Fruit Fly
sources.key_findings: Static connectome as directed message-passing graph with afferent/intrinsic/efferent node types. Integrated with biomechanical fruit fly simulator. Outperforms MLP, random-graph, and degree-preserving-rewired baselines on locomotion tasks. No task-specific architectural tuning needed.
sources.notes: Core inspiration for Project B. Shows that biological graph structure (not just statistics) provides meaningful inductive bias. Directly maps to sensor/inter/motor node type scheme in toy data.

sources.title: Whole-Brain Connectomic Graph Neural Networks Enable Whole-Body Locomotion Control in Drosophila
sources.notes: Earlier NeurIPS version. flyGNN implements connectome as recurrent message-passing network. Demonstrates gait initiation, straight walking, turning. Read alongside FlyGM (2602.17997) to understand architecture evolution.

sources.title: Princeton Neuroscience Institute Summer Internship Program
sources.notes: 9-week program June 1 – July 31. Students placed in PNI labs. Mala Murthy (FlyWire PI) is PNI professor. Apply via Leadership Alliance portal. Personal statement + research interests required. Selection criteria: coding ability, data analysis, capacity for independent progress.

sources.title: FlyWire: online proofreading and visualization platform
sources.notes: Main FlyWire portal. Browse neurons and synapses interactively. Useful for building intuition before running batch analyses.
